articles.title: Pantoja Is the Favorite… But Should He Be?
articles.description: Get in on the fun! The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #DKPartner Alexandre Pantoja is still favored to beat Joshua Van but the betting line is moving. Pantoja opened as a larger favorite, and the gap has tightened as money comes in on Van. Chael Sonnen wants to know why. Was Joshua Van's first victory really a fluke? Chael doesn't buy into that way of looking at competition. Someone won and someone lost, and now they're preparing to do it again. But there is one major variable that could make the rematch different: Pantoja's recovery. Coming back from an injury isn't simply about completing an eight-to-ten-week training camp. Chael explains why a fighter who has been unable to fully practice may need an entire camp just to get into condition to begin a real training camp. Pantoja's discipline isn't the question. His preparation time might be. articles.title: This Is Why I Love Wrestling
articles.description: Sometimes in wrestling, you only need one good day. Chael Sonnen tells the story of Blaine Natal, a wrestler he's known and coached for years. Blaine has spent his life showing up, taking the hard matches and refusing to let failure determine whether he steps on the mat again. His mother, Candy, has been there for all of it. But for all the years of work, Blaine was still waiting for that day. Then he drew Noah Wachsmuth, an undefeated Oregon champion and former Olympic Training Center athlete. On paper, this wasn't supposed to be Blaine's moment. For much of the match, it didn't look like it would be. But wrestling doesn't reward how impressive something looks. The scoreboard does the talking. When time expired, Blaine had one more point. After 22 years, he finally had his day. For Chael, it was one of those rare moments in sports that brought a tear to his eye. You don't need 10 years of perfect days. Sometimes you just need one. articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into two hundred in total bonuses, paid over 21 days. The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #DKPartner Could Tommy “Gun” McMillen become the second-biggest star in UFC history? Conor McGregor remains the standard, but determining who belongs directly behind him is more complicated. Georges St-Pierre produced enormous pay-per-view numbers. Paddy Pimblett has become a massive attraction. Ilia Topuria, Islam Makhachev, Sean O’Malley, Ronda Rousey and Jon Jones all have arguments depending on how stardom is measured. Chael Sonnen believes McMillen could eventually surpass nearly all of them. Tommy has the fighting ability, an authentic personality and the rare ability to deliver a promotional line without making it sound rehearsed. He also trains alongside O’Malley under Tim Welch, giving him access to people who understand that becoming a star requires more than winning fights. McMillen’s undefeated record survived another major test at Noche UFC when he defeated Marwan Rahiki by unanimous decision in a back-and-forth fight. Instead of exposing Tommy, the adversity allowed him to demonstrate toughness, composure and the ability to close strongly. There are still questions. Tommy must continue winning, reach numbered UFC events and discover what will motivate him once the money and attention arrive. But right now, Chael sees no evidence that disqualifies him from becoming the UFC’s next transcendent superstar. articles.title: Ryan Garcia CORRECTLY PREDICTED brutal TKO win vs. Conor Benn | Daniel Cormier
articles.description: In his recent interview with Daniel Cormier, Ryan Garcia TOLD DC he would break Conor Benn's spirit and FINISH HIM in the "first five rounds" with "brutal shots" which is exactly what he did. Hear Garcia tell Cormier how he thought the fight would go down, and why his level would be too much for Benn to handle in this welterweight championship fight.
